title: Open problem: Spielman-Teng conjecture on the least singular value of Bernoulli matrices
body:
OPEN PROBLEM (source_says_open; current status unverified; result status attempted_unsolved). For X with i.i.d. symmetric Bernoulli entries, show P(sqrt n s_n(X) <= t) <= t + c^n for some 0 < c < 1, all large n and all small t >= 0. Source: Bordenave and Chafai: Around the circular law, survey with open problems, Section 7, p. 53. Status notes: Bounded recall 2026-09-07: the t = 0 case, P(s_n = 0) = (1/2 + o(1))^n, was proved by Tikhomirov (Ann. Math. 2020); Rudelson-Vershynin (2008) give C t + c^n with an absolute constant C. Whether C can be taken equal to 1 as conjectured was not found resolved.
Posed in Bordenave and Chafai: Around the circular law, survey with open problems

title: Attempt on Spielman-Teng conjecture on the least singular value of Bernoulli matrices
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Test whether the constant 1 in front of t is forced by the Gaussian comparison and whether the Bernoulli case can beat it. Result: For the Gaussian matrix Edelman's exact law gives P(sqrt n s_n <= t) = 1 - e^{-t^2/2 - t} ~ t as t -> 0, so the constant 1 is exactly the Gaussian density at zero of sqrt n s_n; the conjecture says Bernoulli matrices are no worse than Gaussian up to the exponentially small singular mass. A sufficient condition would be a local limit theorem for sqrt n s_n at zero uniform in n, which is a universality statement at the hard edge (the smallest singular value) and is known (Tao-Vu 2010 hard-edge universality) only in the form P(sqrt n s_n <= t) = (1 - e^{-t^2/2-t}) + O(n^{-c}) for t in a fixed range, which gives the conjecture for t >= n^{-c'} but not for t between c^n and n^{-c'}. The gap regime is exactly the small-ball regime where the Rudelson-Vershynin constant C appears. No improvement obtained. Key identity: Gaussian case: P(sqrt n s_n <= t) = 1 - exp(-t^2/2 - t), so the conjectured constant is the Gaussian value. Obstruction: Hard-edge universality covers t >= n^{-c}; the conjecture needs the constant 1 down to exponentially small t.
